definition: An auxiliary loss (or loss-free bias method) that pushes the router to spread tokens across experts, preventing a few experts from absorbing all traffic while others go untrained.
details: An auxiliary loss (or loss-free bias method) that pushes the router to spread tokens across experts, preventing a few experts from absorbing all traffic while others go untrained.

explainer.lead: Load balancing loss is an auxiliary objective that pushes a mixture-of-experts router to spread tokens across experts. It matters because without it a few experts absorb all traffic while the rest never train.

tiers.eli5: If everyone queues at one checkout, the other tills stay idle; this is a nudge that spreads shoppers evenly across the tills.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers add it as a small penalty term during MoE training, or use a loss-free bias method; a pitfall is setting the weight too high, which forces tokens onto poorly suited experts.
tiers.paperLevel: An auxiliary loss added to the training objective that penalises uneven token distribution across experts; alternatively, a loss-free bias method adjusts routing biases directly. The trade-off is between routing balance and task loss.

explainer.example: A router sends 90 percent of tokens to two of sixteen experts, so the balancing term raises the loss and training shifts traffic toward the idle experts.
